scopePolicy: The audited boundary is every named semantic control plus every stored field of the immutable score, articulation, instrument, composition, material-world, DSP-graph, spatial, mix, live-master, repeat-hold, and future-adaptation types that currently carry musical or signal-processing intent across the canonical Core-to-DSP-to-evidence path. Local variables, derived evidence/report payloads, transport counters, caches, raw PCM containers, and implementation coefficients that never cross an owner boundary are not parameter state; their safety remains owned by their focused DSP and evaluator tests.

domains.title: Active semantic intent controls
domains.limitations: The audit composes exact mapper consumption with downstream score/render tests; it does not claim an independent full-phrase scalar sweep for all eighteen correlated controls.

domains.title: Quarantined intent-only control
domains.limitations: This historical value mutates typed plan identity but has no scene, PCM, signal-evidence, or controller consequence. It is retained only as an explicit quarantine until an engine/provenance migration can remove it without silently invalidating calibrated identities.

domains.title: Quarantined score-only sequencer surface
domains.limitations: These controls produce bounded score metadata and typed fingerprints, but no canonical renderer consumes the events and no signal evidence or bounded future decision observes a consequence. The audit prevents that dormant surface from being mistaken for implemented synthesis.

domains.title: Scene, rhythm, motif, and derived render character
domains.limitations: Seed and tempo are structural/provenance members within the same immutable scene root; their replay and fixed-tempo contracts are tested separately from musical scalar causality.

domains.title: Performance identity and resolved score
domains.limitations: Collection and provenance members are covered through exact plan fingerprints and preflight completeness in addition to representative direct event PCM mutation.

domains.title: Physical and relational bar articulations
domains.limitations: Each articulation family owns separate focused causal tests; this row uses groove pulse as the representative anchor while the generated member table prevents hidden fields.

domains.title: Instrument assignment and upper performance
domains.limitations: Role-specific tests isolate timbre, timing, tail, pump, reveal, and echo consequences; the domain-level PCM anchor is not a replacement for those focused tests.

domains.title: Kick and modal physical-model parameters
domains.limitations: Kick and modal members have separate causal suites; the row's representative kick test is supplemented by ModalPercussionDSPTests and candidate completeness checks.

domains.title: Phrase composition and accepted-memory parameters
domains.limitations: Slice, arpeggiator, pad-harmony, pad-rhythm, and memory paths have different focused PCM tests; the member inventory is complete while the displayed anchor is representative.

domains.title: Long-horizon material, effect, energy, and polymetric parameters
domains.limitations: Long-horizon members include lineage and boundary provenance as well as PCM-bearing targets; exact typed fingerprints distinguish those roles.

domains.title: DSP graph and spatial-network contracts
domains.limitations: Configuration includes derived frame counts and feedback gains; constructors and route-normalized stability tests are the authority for those derived members.

domains.title: Automatic mix and live-master controller parameters
domains.limitations: Automatic mix is detached render-state adaptation while live master crosses an App-authoritative future boundary; they share a domain only as attenuation-only controllers and retain separate tests.

domains.title: Repeat-hold transformation and future-adaptation parameters
domains.limitations: Repeat-hold filters transform already-qualified PCM without canonical score advance; future-adaptation state changes only unstarted plans. The report keeps those consequences distinct despite their shared future-boundary role.
